title: Martial Havoc content file
description: The one schema every data file in packages/content/data validates against. A file is an envelope (id, kind, title, cite, label, docs) wrapping an array of records. `kind` names the shape of the table's dice address; the top-level oneOf switches on it, and each branch fixes exactly which record shapes that kind may hold. Every object is closed (additionalProperties: false) so a stray or misspelled field is red, and every record carries `id` and `cite` so nothing ships without a folio. Phase 5's adventure files reuse these same kinds, which is what keeps `one schema` true.

id.description: Dotted kebab-case identifier, unique across the whole package (e.g. `technique.iron-head`). The d66 or the band is a field, never part of the id.

cite.description: Where the record comes from: a folio (`MH p.12`), an inventory id (`I-04`), or a repo path.

label.description: The spec's three labels. Every table transcribed from the book is `rule`.

reading.description: An inventory reading id, carried IN ADDITION to the record's own fields when a cell is inferred rather than printed. Never instead of `cite`.

band.description: A banded d6 address as printed: the first die's range (`1-2`, `3-4`, `5-6`, or `1-3`, `4-6`).

d66.description: A d66 address: tens die then ones die, read as a two-digit number (11..66; every digit is 1-6, which the content test asserts).

faces.description: The d6 faces a banded row covers, listed explicitly so the engine never parses a range string.

diceSpec.description: A dice expression as data: `n` dice of `d` faces plus `plus`. `n: 0` means no dice at all, so a fixed amount (Vagabond's 1 GP) needs no second shape and no branch in the engine.

namedValue.description: A Proficiency (or Technique/Ritual) name with the value printed beside it.

martialArt.description: One of the 18 Martial Arts (MH p.7-10), banded d6 x d6. `power` is the style text's own power where the style carries one (R13), verbatim, else null.

deity.description: One of the 12 Deities (MH p.29), banded d6 x d6; three columns combine into a name.

finalBlow.description: One of the 18 Final Blow inspiration rows (MH p.26), banded d6 x d6: an action, an attribute and an animal to name a landed blow (R31).

cityEncounter.description: One of the 12 city-encounter rows (MH p.51), banded d6 x d6: how the person you already know is connected to you, and one trait.

learnable.description: A Technique (MH p.12-15) or a Ritual (MH p.16-19) on its d66 address. `cost` is both the Resource points to learn (R16) and the ENDURANCE to perform (R18). `effect` and `pinyin` are verbatim, non-standard spellings included.

d66Text.description: A d66 row whose whole content is one passage of text (the 36 adventure hooks, MH p.36-39).

word.description: One word cell of a d66 word table: the two Inspirations tables (MH p.59-60, `table` is `action` or `theme`) and the six Sparks tables (MH p.60-63, `table` is `1`..`6`).

socialStatus.description: One of the 5 social-status bands (MH p.5, R03): the faces that land on it, the status name, and the gold it starts you with as a dice spec.

treasure.description: One cell of the Treasure table (MH p.68, R78): 1d6 down the side, the defeated opponent's ENDURANCE band across the top.

unexpectedEvent.description: One row of the Unexpected Event table (MH p.28, R32). `retreatRow` marks the two Enemy-retreat rows: the sealed Morale reading lives on them and reopens only through /re-seed.

specialItem.description: One row of the Special Items table (MH p.69, R79), 2d6. `effect` is verbatim, lower-case openings included.

exceptionalWeapon.description: One weapon that passes R77's gate against an incorporeal opponent (MH p.66). The rule names the category and lists no members; reading I-29 names these three. `ref` is the id of the record that already holds the weapon - a Special Item, an adventure treasure, or the preset sheet that carries it as an equipment line - so the name is transcribed once and this file only says which of them the gate opens for.

ref.description: The id of the record that holds this weapon.

note.description: Why this one counts, in one line.

encounterCell.description: One cell of the Encounters matrix (MH p.67, R74): a 2d6 total in one of the five columns. `printed` is the cell verbatim; `opponentRef` is the canonical opponent id it resolves to, or null when the cell redirects to another column instead of naming an opponent.

columnCell.description: One cell of a d6-per-column table: the Region table (MH p.43) and the Monastery table (MH p.45). Roll one d6 for each column you need.

oracleCell.description: One cell of the Oracle (MH p.58, R71): 11 named rows, one d6 across. `spanInferred` is true where the printed cell is centred under two or more faces and the estate inferred the span; the text is the same in every face of that span.

opponent.description: One of the 50 opponent stat blocks (MH p.70-79, R80). `attack` is printed as an integer, as the range `2-4` (Brawler), or blank (Huang Feng Guai) - kept as printed rather than normalised. `martialArtsValue` carries the n of a `Martial Arts (n)` Proficiency (R75); the Proficiency itself stays in the list. `incorporeal` is the R77 gate's data side: true for the spirits and ghosts reading I-29 names, false everywhere else; a tagged record also carries `reading: "I-29"`, since no cell of the printed stat block says it.

incorporeal.description: Immune to ordinary blows (R77): only a Technique, a Ritual or an exceptional weapon can hurt it. Read (never recomputed) by the engine's `ordinaryBlowsPass`.

marketItem.description: One priced line of the four Market lists (MH p.52-55). Exactly one of `priceGp` / `priceSp` is set, as printed. `flags` is computed at data time and read (never recomputed) by the engine: `weapon` (R68, I-02), `underTwentyGp` (the starting-kit cap of R02), `alcohol` (I-03).

cityService.description: One line of the City Services price list (MH p.50, R64). The price is kept verbatim because the list prices per question, per dose, per day and per km, and one line is a range (`50-200 GP`) and one is `free offering`.

healing.description: One row of the healing summary (MH p.31, R40-R42): what partially restores an attribute, by how much, and what fully restores it. LUCK has no full-restore rule, so `full` is null.

xpCategory.description: One of the end-of-adventure score categories (MH p.34, R43). `max` is null for the Dishonor line, which is subtracted and unbounded.

xpCost.description: One cell of the XP cost table (MH p.34, R44): what +1 of `increase` costs at the given current-SKILL band.

band.description: One band of a banded roll whose whole content is one label: route type on 2d6 and road features on 1d6 (MH p.44, R54-R55). `totals` lists the results that land on the band explicitly, so nothing parses a range at runtime.

preset.description: One of Appendix C's eight ready-to-play Master sheets (MH p.91-92, R83), transcribed field for field. Spelling is the sheets' own; names resolve to canonical table ids through the file's `nameResolution` map. Yin's overspends and Sun Wukong's out-of-range implied SKILL are recorded, never corrected.

string.description: One UI string of the app shell. The only record kind that is ours rather than the book's, which is why its file is labelled `invention`.

effect.description: One authored effect record for a Technique or a Ritual (MH p.12-19; reading A23). The printed effect text stays verbatim in `techniques.json` / `rituals.json`; this record points at it by `ref` and says what it does at the table. A23 is the inventory's one row with no defensible inference, so every record here is an invention of this build, cited to it.

ref.description: The id of the transcribed Technique or Ritual this record is the effect of. Must resolve; the content test checks it.

cost.description: Resource points to learn, ENDURANCE to perform (R16, R18). Copied from the referenced record; the test pins the two together.

timing.description: When it may be used. A Technique is `immediate` outside combat and `combat-winner-option` inside it (R14, R25, I-23); a Ritual is `preparation` - not usable during combat rounds, costing a scene (I-24). `scene` is for effects that occupy a scene without the Ritual's preparation.

operation.description: The engine operation the class implies, as a dotted name (e.g. `combat.opening`, `healing.endurance`). Null for narrative-only effects, which is most of them.

wudangException.description: True for the Ritual timing exception R13 grants Wudang. A flag on the record so the engine holds no style name.

line.description: The authored line - what the table reads when the effect fires. Ours, never a paraphrase of the printed effect.

authoredLine.description: One authored line for a transcribed record that prints none: an Oracle cell (MH p.58) or an Unexpected Event row (MH p.28). The cell's own words stay verbatim where they are; this is the sentence the table reads aloud when it comes up.

ref.description: The id of the transcribed record this line belongs to. Must resolve; the content test checks it.

line.description: The authored line. Ours, never a paraphrase of the transcribed text.

beat.description: One area of an adventure as the beat screen shows it: the printed area name and an authored line of ours read when the Master stands there (spec.md, Horizon: an authored line beside every menu). The area's printed description stays in docs/ until Phase 5's adventure format transcribes it; this record is the prototype slice.

area.description: The area's printed number (1-8 in The 5 Treasures).

line.description: The authored line. Ours, never a paraphrase of the printed description.

menuOption.description: One entry of the beat menu: what the rules allow the Master to do in an area, the authored line beside it, and the engine action it triggers. The menu is the app's whole grammar of play (spec.md, Horizon), so every entry is data with a citation.

area.description: The area this option is offered in.

note.description: The short mechanical note printed beside the title (SKILL CHECK, +4 END, AREA 3).

action.description: The engine action the option performs. The app's reducer switches on it and nothing else.

target.description: What the action acts on: an area number for `go`, a foe id for `fight`, a treasure key for `take`.

proficiency.description: For `skill-check`: the name of the one Proficiency that adds to the threshold (R20, D10). Omitted for a bare SKILL check.

behaviourNote.description: The rules panel's note on one engine behaviour: what the engine does, in a sentence, and for a reading the four questions the panel asks (what the book says, what it is silent on, the source, what reversing it would change). `ref` is the behaviour id in the engine registry; scripts/labels-check.test.ts holds the two in step.

ref.description: The engine behaviour id this note describes (e.g. `combat.final-blow-doubles`).

says.description: What the book prints on the point, quoted or summarised.

silent.description: What the book does not say, which is why a position had to be taken.

reversed.description: What changes if the position is reversed.

adventureMeta.description: The header record of one adventure written in the adventure format (packages/content/schema/adventure-format.md). Exactly one per adventure directory: the format version its files are written in, the printed title, the premise paragraph verbatim, the area the Master starts in, and the printed credit line. Every other file of the adventure names this record's id in its own `adventure` field, which is what makes the directory one document.

version.description: The adventure format version this adventure is written in. Bumped only when a record shape changes incompatibly; the engine refuses a version it does not know.

premise.description: The premise paragraph, verbatim. Never a paraphrase: the printed prose is the adventure's opening screen.

startArea.description: The id of the area the Master begins in (an `adventureArea` record id).

credits.description: The licence and credit line, verbatim.

adventureArea.description: One area of an adventure: its printed number and title, its printed description, its spoiler-gated Hint, an authored line of ours for the beat screen, the areas it leads to, the lock on entering it, and the treasures lying in it. Description and hint are verbatim transcriptions; `line` is the only authored field.

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this area belongs to.

area.description: The area's printed number (1-8 in The 5 Treasures).

description.description: The area's printed description, verbatim, printed spelling and all.

hint.description: The grey Hint paragraph, verbatim. Hidden until earned (I-60): revealed by an Event roll of 6, or by information about the area (I-06b).

line.description: The authored line read when the Master stands here. Ours, never a paraphrase of the printed description.

exits.description: The ids of the areas reachable from here. Undirected in the source; listed once per area in both directions.

gate.description: The lock on entering this area, or null where the way in is open. `key` is a key id an `adventureLoot` row can drop; `text` is what the door is, as the source describes it.

treasures.description: Treasure ids found here by exploration rather than as loot (I-38). Empty for most areas.

rescue.description: A stat-blocked NPC who is a rescue rather than an enemy (I-39): fightable if the Master attacks, otherwise freed for the reward of their loot roll. Null in every area that holds none.

dishonorOnAttack.description: True where attacking the rescue costs the Master honour rather than earning a fight.

adventureEncounter.description: One row of an area's encounter table: which 1d6 faces land on it, which foes are met, and how many. `faces: []` is a fixed encounter - an area whose printed Encounters line carries no dice (I-34), met on any Ambush or Encounter event. `empty: true` is a row that meets nothing (I-36).

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this row belongs to.

area.description: The printed number of the area whose table this row is in.

faces.description: The 1d6 faces that land on this row, listed explicitly so nothing parses a range at runtime. Empty for a fixed encounter.

foes.description: The foe ids met on this row. Two ids is a multiple combat (R35), as the Attendants room's `Both`.

count.description: How many of each foe: `one` a single opponent; `band` a group that attacks together (I-05b); `oracle` a number read from the Oracle's No. of enemies row (I-34); `none` where the row meets nothing.

empty.description: True where the row meets nothing and the event degrades to Safe exploration (I-36).

adventureLoot.description: One row of a foe's printed LOOT line. A line with dice becomes one record per band; a line naming a single item becomes one record with `faces: []`. `treasure` and `key` lift a drop out of plain text into something the engine can hold.

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this row belongs to.

foe.description: The opponent id whose LOOT line this row is part of.

faces.description: The 1d6 faces that land on this row; empty where the line names a single drop with no roll.

treasure.description: The treasure id where this drop is one of the adventure's named treasures, else null.

key.description: The key id where this drop opens a gate, else null. Two foes may drop the same key id (I-07).

hint.description: True where the printed drop is the warning-triangle icon with no text, read as a Hint (I-08).

once.description: True where the drop is unique in the adventure and cannot be had twice (I-33c: the seven-star sword drops once).

adventureTreasure.description: One of the adventure's named treasures: its printed name and its printed effect, where it is found, and what reveals how it works. The effect is spoiler-gated like a Hint (I-60): hidden until the treasure is acquired, or until something in `knownFrom` is read.

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this treasure belongs to.

effect.description: How the treasure works, verbatim from the spoiler-gated section.

source.description: `area` where the treasure is picked up by exploration (I-38); `loot` where it is a foe's drop.

sourceRef.description: The area id or the foe id named by `source`.

knownFrom.description: Ids that reveal this treasure's effect without acquiring it - an area whose sheets explain it (I-38b), a foe who knows the spells (I-41). Empty means the effect is revealed on acquiring.

adventureFlag.description: One per-adventure flag: a named boolean the areas and the encounter tables read. The adventure has a clock and states where the rulebook has none (I-40), and every one of them is data rather than a branch in the engine.

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this flag belongs to.

flag.description: The flag's name, as the engine reads it.

initial.description: The flag's value when the adventure begins.

text.description: What the flag means, in one line.

adventureAbsence.description: One rule of the form `while this flag holds, this foe is not met in this area`. The adventure's only such rule is the Cave entrance's Ogres, who hunt once a day and so are absent by night (I-45); the shape exists so a second adventure states its own without an engine change.

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this rule belongs to.

area.description: The printed number of the area the foe is absent from, or 0 for every area of the adventure.

foe.description: The opponent id that is not met.

whenTrue.description: The flag value that makes the foe absent.

adventureAct.description: One act marker of an adventure: the condition that advances the Master into it and the authored line the marker reads. The last row carries `ending: true` and is the ending screen - the thing a scripted playthrough has to reach for the adventure to be finishable.

adventure.description: The `adventureMeta` id this act belongs to.

act.description: The act's number, ascending from 1. Acts are tested in order and the highest satisfied one is current.

condition.description: What advances into this act: `start` always holds; `enter` an area has been entered; `defeated` a foe has been defeated; `treasures` at least n treasures are held.

threshold.description: What the condition tests: a count for `treasures`, an area or foe id for `enter` and `defeated`, null for `start`.

line.description: The authored line the marker reads. Ours.

ending.description: True on exactly one row per adventure: the ending screen.

villagePlace.description: One place in the trail-head village (spec.md, Horizon: "a trail-head village is a City on fixed data"). The village is an invention of this build - the rulebook describes a City (MH p.46-51) and the adventure describes a mountain, neither describes this settlement - so every record here is cited to the Horizon, while the procedure each place runs is the book's. A `location` is somewhere the Master stands and acts; the single `trail` is the departure edge out of the village, and it names the adventure it leads to rather than running a procedure.

kind.description: `location` is a place with a procedure; `trail` is the way out.

name.description: The place's authored name. Ours (invention), never a transcription.

blurb.description: The authored sentence a screen reads when the Master stands here. Copy lives here, never in a component (agents.md rule 7).

procedure.description: Which engine procedure this place runs, or null for the trail. `buy` is the Market table at printed prices (MH p.52-55); `temple` is the Spirituality check for +1 LUCK (R58, I-58); `inn` is a meal and a night's rest (R40; spec.md's sealed +4 ENDURANCE).

destination.description: For a `trail`, the `adventureMeta` id it leads to. Null for a location.

roomPriceSp.description: The inn's price for a bed and a meal, in silver pieces (1 GP = 10 SP, MH p.52). Invented: the book prices no inn. Null everywhere else.

nameResolution.description: Sheet spelling to canonical id. The sheets abbreviate and re-capitalise; this map is how a preset's free text becomes a table lookup without editing what the sheet prints.

docs.description: Optional for this kind only: the app strings have no docs/ concept behind them.
